notice: Simulation with synthetic patients and stated assumptions; not a clinical trial.

personas.summary: Replies to the first message and takes the first slot that fits.
personas.rationale: ASSUMPTION: the largest group. Most patients who read a message from their own clinic answer it, and many of them would have done the order anyway (high self-completion).

personas.summary: Misses the first message, answers a later one.
personas.rationale: ASSUMPTION: busy patients who read messages late; a second contact several days later is what gets an answer.

personas.summary: Answers, but the offered time never suits them ("not Tuesday", only Saturdays).
personas.rationale: ASSUMPTION: working patients for whom weekday mornings do not work; they book when the time changes, and rarely find a time on their own after a generic reminder.

personas.summary: The phone on file is wrong: messages are undelivered until reception fixes it.
personas.rationale: ASSUMPTION: outdated or mistyped numbers. Once the right number is found they behave like an average patient.

personas.summary: Reads messages but never answers them; a phone call from reception works.
personas.rationale: ASSUMPTION: patients who do not write back to a clinic but pick up the phone.

personas.summary: Never answers a message or a call.
personas.rationale: ASSUMPTION: disengaged patients. Nothing in either arm reaches them; they complete an order only on their own.

personas.summary: Asks the clinic to stop writing at the first reply.
personas.rationale: ASSUMPTION: a small share of patients do not want messages; both arms stop writing to them.

personas.summary: Did the test at an outside lab; sends a photo of the result when asked.
personas.rationale: ASSUMPTION: patients who use a cheaper or closer lab. The clinic never receives that result unless someone asks for it; asked, most send a photo.

assumptions: ASSUMPTION: the persona mix and every probability in this file are plausible values chosen by the team, not measurements, and no study is cited for them. A clinic's own control group (V2 PRD, workstream B) replaces them with measured outcomes.

ASSUMPTION: without any contact, a share of patients completes each order on their own (from 10 % to 60 % by persona); urgent visits half as often, because the patient does not know the result is abnormal. The same draw applies in both arms.

ASSUMPTION: the control arm is usual care with fixed reminders: one generic message when the order is due and one 7 days later, no booking help, no follow-up calls, no way to send a result back. A patient who engages books or goes to the lab on their own (with the persona's probability).

ASSUMPTION: reception completes 90 % of the agent's call tasks on their due day; 80 % of the patients who answer a call book on it. Clinic capacity is not a constraint: every patient sees the synthetic schedule's free slots.
ASSUMPTION: every result is normal, so a result never opens a new abnormal follow-up during the window.

SIMPLIFICATION: the patient's side of the conversation is the persona model, not a language model. The agent's policy is the real code: the ladder, the urgent and undelivered tracks, the contact cap (2 proactive messages per 7 days) and the slots of packages/core/src/engine/order-agent.
SIMPLIFICATION: the agent takes a test or an urgent visit at once, and a control visit 14 days before it is due (the order agent has no start rule of its own yet).
AS IN THE AGENT: once an order is booked the agent stops chasing it, even when the patient does not show up; a no-show is not recovered by the agent.
ENGINE RULE: a visit order closes on a booking made in time and opens again when the booking date passes with no visit. "Fulfilled" is the engine's own status of the order at day 90.
ECONOMICS: recovered revenue counts only attended consultations (agent minus control) at the configured price, USD 40 by default; lab and imaging revenue is not counted.
